dataFlowTrace.literal: loadAsync defaults: checkCRC32 false, createFolders false, utf8 name decoding. ZipEntries.load: EOCD located by lastIndexOfSignature, garbage vs truncated distinguished (zipEntries.js:156-173), zip64 locator/record supported with the 53-bit caveat, multi-volume rejected (109), central-directory loop bounded by signature matches with record-count sanity check (141-151), negative extra-bytes rejected (242-244), local header per entry re-checked (115-125). Every read is bounds-checked (DataReader.checkIndex throws 'End of data reached ... Corrupted zip ?'). Encrypted entries rejected (zipEntry.js:121-123), unknown compression rejected (92-95). Entry names normalized by utils.resolve (dot and dot-dot segments) with unsafeOriginalName retained (load.js). Compressed bytes are referenced at load (readData(compressedSize)); decompression is lazy per .async(). Copy-vs-view semantics of readData not verified.
dataFlowTrace.mitigation: Structural rejection of non-zip, truncated, encrypted, unknown-method and multi-volume input happens before any inflate; errors surface as rejections.

dataFlowTrace.location: mammoth lib/docx/docx-reader.js read/findPartPaths; lib/zipfile.js read; jszip zipObject.js, compressedObject.js, stream/DataWorker.js, flate.js, stream/StreamHelper.js
dataFlowTrace.literal: Parts read: [Content_Types].xml, _rels/.rels, main-document rels, the main document part (relationship target normalized and existence-checked, else fallback word/document.xml; missing -> 'Could not find main document part'), styles, numbering, footnotes, endnotes, comments, each with its own .rels. Each read inflates the whole part: DataWorker emits 16 KiB input chunks, one per setImmediate tick (utils.delay -> setimmediate polyfill), FlateWorker runs pako raw inflate per chunk, StreamHelper.accumulate concatenates into one Uint8Array, DataLengthProbe compares to the header uncompressedSize only after inflate completes ('Bug : uncompressed data size mismatch'). No cap on the inflated size exists in app or library code; the only input bound is the 5 MiB compressed gate.
dataFlowTrace.mitigation: Inflate is interleaved with the event loop at chunk granularity; mismatched size headers are detected post hoc; CRC is not checked (default off, mammoth does not enable it).

dataFlowTrace.location: mammoth lib/docx/office-xml-reader.js readXmlFromZipFile; lib/xml/reader.js; lib/xml/xmldom.js; @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15 lib/dom-parser.js:75-129, lib/sax.js:60-76 and 590-611
dataFlowTrace.literal: TextDecoder('utf-8') decode, BOM strip, then mammoth's wrapper parses with an errorHandler callback; buildErrorHandler (dom-parser.js:116-127) routes warning, error and fatalError to that callback, and the wrapper throws on any of them, so any xmldom diagnostic rejects the whole extraction (reader.js catches and rejects). Entities: entityReplacer resolves only the predefined XML entity map and numeric references; an undefined entity raises 'entity not found' -> rejection. DOCTYPE: the header name/PUBLIC/SYSTEM tokens are passed to startDTD/endDTD; no code path in the sections read registers internal-subset entity declarations. No fetch/XMLHttpRequest/fs/http usage exists anywhere in xmldom lib (grep). CDATA handled. Parsing is synchronous for the whole part string; mammoth then converts the DOM recursively (reader.js convertNode/convertElement) and collapses mc:AlternateContent to mc:Fallback.
dataFlowTrace.mitigation: External entity resolution is impossible by construction in the code read; malformed XML fails closed rather than degrading silently.

supportedLimitsAndMitigations: 5 MiB compressed-size gate before any read; extension allowlist of four types; both unit-tested at the boundary.

Processing is browser-local on the read path: no network or filesystem API in resume.ts, mammoth lib (lib/main.js, lib/unzip.js, lib/docx/files.js require fs but are the Node variants replaced or unused in the browser build), xmldom lib, or the jszip files read.
JSZip rejects non-zip, truncated, encrypted, unknown-compression and multi-volume input with bounds-checked header parsing and normalizes entry names.
Mammoth fails closed on any XML diagnostic, requires the main document part, and never reads image bytes for raw text.
xmldom resolves predefined and numeric entities only and has no external-entity or network capability in the code read.

Applied text is capped at 50,000 UTF-16 units; derived profile fields are length- and class-bounded; resume text is never persisted; only the Profile object is stored and it is schema-validated on load.
Cancellation removes listeners, discards stale results, and aborts on unmount; the UI cannot be overwritten by a replaced or cancelled read.
unverifiedOrHypothetical: Decompression expansion: the 5 MiB gate bounds compressed input only. The inflated size of the XML parts mammoth reads is bounded by the deflate format and header values, not by any app or library cap, and the length check runs after inflate. Peak heap and duration are unmeasured; no browser freeze or out-of-memory claim is made.
Main-thread phases (TextDecoder, xmldom parse, element conversion, body reading, raw-text join) are synchronous per part while inflate yields per 16 KiB chunk; responsiveness impact is unmeasured.
Unbounded concurrency of replaced extractions is a literal property of the code; its resource impact is unmeasured.

Deep XML nesting drives recursion in three places (reader.js convertNode, body-reader readXmlElements, raw-text convertElementToRawText); an engine stack overflow would be thrown inside a promise chain and surface as the error path. Not tested, not measured.
Regex work in analyzeResume runs over up to 50,000 units per analyze click; per-line application and bounded groups were observed, timing was not measured.
Advisory status of mammoth 1.12.3, jszip 3.10.2, @xmldom/xmldom 0.8.15 and pako 1.0.11 was not queried; no vulnerability or severity is inferred from versions or source patterns.
Raw library error text reaching the alert is a literal information/UX observation, not a confirmed security impact.
Content-fidelity notes (hidden runs included, tracked deletions excluded, notes/comments/headers excluded) are behavior observations, not security findings.
